title: Deep Learning for Subgrid-Scale Turbulence Modeling in Large-Eddy Simulations of the Convective Atmospheric Boundary Layer
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
host_model: Pseudospectral/finite-difference LES solver (Kumar et al., 2006; Li et al., 2018)
testbed_rationale: High-fidelity DNS data across varying stability regimes (from shear-dominated to highly convective) are filtered and made publicly available at a persistent DOI for testing and benchmarking ML subgrid-scale turbulence closures.
pain_points: Numerical vs. physical dissipation balance in online LES coupling
Aliasing errors when coarse-graining DNS data can inadvertently be learned by neural networks
Coupling stability at the lowest surface boundaries requires ad-hoc smoothing/averaging with Monin-Obukhov similarity theory
Difficulty generalizing to different boundary conditions (e.g., channel flow vs. ABL)
extraction_notes: The DNN architecture utilizes local 3D stencils (e.g., 3x3x3 neighboring grid cells) to emulate spatial gradient/convolution operations without assuming eddy viscosity. Online coupling in LES demonstrated stability and preserved the -5/3 energy cascade spectrum.
